<explanation>
Below is a tailored set of instructions for drawing a system‐design diagram of the Wav2Lip project. We have broken the system into its core components, shown how data and control flow between them, and highlighted the key architectural patterns and dependencies. Follow these guidelines to produce a clear, accurate, and detailed diagram.

1. Identify the Main Components  
   a. Data Ingestion & Preprocessing  
      • Raw video + audio files  
      • `preprocess.py` reads `filelists/` → generates face crops (`.jpg`) + audio (`.wav`) under `lrs2_preprocessed/`  
   b. Face Detection Module  
      • `face_detection/api.py` & `face_detection/detection/sfd` (S3FD)  
      • Takes raw frames → returns bounding boxes → crops passed to next stage  
   c. Expert Discriminator (SyncNet) Training  
      • `color_syncnet_train.py`  
      • Uses PyTorch model in `models/syncnet.py`  
      • Trains SyncNet (“expert lip‐sync discriminator”) on preprocessed data → saves checkpoints in `checkpoints/`  
   d. Wav2Lip Model Training  
      • Two scripts:  
         – `wav2lip_train.py` (base model)  
         – `hq_wav2lip_train.py` (with visual‐quality GAN discriminator)  
      • Underlying model in `models/wav2lip.py`  
      • Reads SyncNet checkpoint, preprocessed data → outputs Wav2Lip checkpoints  
   e. Inference Pipeline  
      • `inference.py`  
      • Inputs: arbitrary video (`--face`), audio (`--audio`), Wav2Lip checkpoint  
      • Invokes face detection → crops + audio → Wav2Lip model → merges generated frames + audio → writes to `results/`  
   f. Evaluation & Metrics  
      • `evaluation/` folder  
      • Scripts to compute LSE‐D, LSE‐C, PSNR, SSIM, etc.  
      • Reads generated videos from `results/` and reference lists from `evaluation/test_filelists/`  
   g. Checkpoints & Results Storage  
      • `checkpoints/` stores all training checkpoints  
      • `results/` stores inference outputs  

2. Draw Relationships & Data Flow  
   • Arrow: Raw data (video/audio) → Preprocessing → Preprocessed dataset  
   • Arrow: Preprocessed dataset → SyncNet training → SyncNet checkpoint  
   • Arrow: Preprocessed dataset + SyncNet checkpoint → Wav2Lip training → Wav2Lip checkpoint  
   • Arrow: Any input video/audio + Wav2Lip checkpoint → Inference → Generated video  
   • Arrow: Generated video + test filelists → Evaluation scripts → Metrics & scores  

3. Highlight Architectural Patterns & Design Principles  
   • Modular separation:  
     – Data preparation (`preprocess.py`)  
     – Model training (SyncNet vs Wav2Lip)  
     – Inference (`inference.py`)  
     – Evaluation (`evaluation/`)  
   • Reusable components: face detection API isolated under `face_detection/`  
   • Centralized hyperparameters: `hparams.py`  
   • Extensibility points: new discriminators, custom datasets via `filelists/`  

4. Annotate Key Technologies  
   • Python 3.6, PyTorch, ffmpeg  
   • Face detection: S3FD (from `face_detection/detection/sfd`)  
   • Models:  
     – `models/syncnet.py`  
     – `models/wav2lip.py`  
     – (Optional) Conv blocks in `models/conv.py`  
   • External storage: Google Drive links for pretrained weights  

5. Tailor Diagram to an Open-Source ML Toolkit  
   • Emphasize:  
     – Core functionality modules (preprocess, train, infer, eval)  
     – Data flow between them  
     – Hooks for external datasets via `filelists/`  
     – Checkpoint management under `checkpoints/`  

6. Diagramming Guidelines  
   • Use clear, rectangular boxes for components (e.g., “Preprocessor”, “SyncNet Trainer”, “Wav2Lip Model”)  
   • Label each box with script names and directory paths where appropriate  
   • Draw directional arrows to show:  
     – Data flow (videos/audio → modules → outputs)  
     – Dependency flow (SyncNet checkpoint → Wav2Lip training)  
   • Color‐code or shape‐code:  
     – Data stores (e.g., filelists, checkpoints, results) in one color/shape  
     – Compute modules (training, inference) in another  
     – External dependencies (ffmpeg, Google Drive) in a third  
   • Include a legend that maps colors/shapes to component types  

7. Don’t Overthink—Separate Into As Many Logical Components As Possible  
   • Treat each script or directory as its own module if it encapsulates a distinct responsibility  
   • Explicitly show:  
     – Data inputs/outputs (raw folders, preprocessed folders)  
     – Model artifacts (checkpoint files)  
     – Evaluation metrics outputs  

By following the above breakdown and visualization rules, you will end up with a highly detailed, precise architecture diagram of the Wav2Lip system—clearly showing how data moves through preprocessing, face detection, model training, inference, and evaluation, as well as how all major scripts, directories, and external dependencies interact.
